title: Strings: working with text
objective: Combine text values together to form new sentences.
explanation_md:
## Strings

Any piece of text in Python is called a **string**. Strings always go inside quotes.

```python
greeting = "Hello"
name = "Sam"
```

### Joining strings (concatenation)

You can stick strings together with the `+` symbol:

```python
full = greeting + ", " + name
print(full)   # Hello, Sam
```

### f-strings (the modern way)

It is often nicer to use an **f-string**. Put `f` before the opening quote and use `{ }` to drop a variable in:

```python
name = "Sam"
print(f"Hello, {name}!")
```

Both approaches give the same result.

## Your turn

Make two variables: `first` set to your first name, and `last` set to your last name (any names, they're just strings). Then print: 

> `Hello, FIRST LAST!`

Use a single space between first and last, and end with an exclamation mark.

For the auto-check, please use `first = "Ada"` and `last = "Lovelace"` so the output is `Hello, Ada Lovelace!`.
